answer.answer: Straylight is not currently ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth. The 2026-07-26 current-status note controls because it explicitly supersedes the 2026-07-23 green checkpoint. Production-scale retrieval can exceed the 30-second database timeout, shared transactions can erase a successful retrieval lane when a later lane fails, and normal writes copy the full corpus membership manifest. The approved direction is a Markdown-as-truth architecture with changed-file-only versioning, rebuildable derived state, precise checkpoint references, coherent hydration, and compact retrieval packets.

claims.value: Projects/Straylight current status.md controls: it was updated 2026-07-26T12:00:00-07:00 and explicitly supersedes Projects/Straylight stale checkpoint.md. The older note was recorded 2026-07-23T18:00:00-07:00 and labels its healthy retrieval test, healthy `/ready`, and immediate owner-alpha recommendation as historical evidence that predates the production-sized timeout and full-manifest-copy findings and must not override the newer note.

Production retrieval is not dependable at owner scale: although connection, authentication, and exact-path reads work, the owner corpus contains about 64,000 active records and 9.6 million estimated source tokens; broad `memory.open` and lexical retrieval are slow and can hit the 30-second database timeout. Because retrieval lanes share one transaction, a later lane failure can discard an earlier successful lane. The current architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth.

Normal writes copy a full corpus membership manifest, making an ordinary write produce a corpus-wide manifest copy instead of versioning only the changed file. This production-scale write-amplification finding supersedes the older green checkpoint’s readiness conclusion.

The approved simplification is to make current Markdown files the workspace truth; version only changed files; make indexes and derived views rebuildable; checkpoint with exact path, version, and hash references plus changes since a workspace generation; and retain coherent source hydration and compact retrieval packets. This is an approved direction, not verified completed implementation.
